    Paid tax by mistake and the Income Tax department refused your refund? You can still claim it back. Here’s exactly how Vijay did it: Meet Varun Hemant Keskar. 🔸 He is an NRI living and working in Singapore 🔸 He has a valid Tax Residency Certificate from Singapore for FY 2023-24 🔸 He invested in Indian mutual funds 🔸 He sold some of them and made capital gains 🔸 He paid ₹1.70 lakh capital gains tax to the Indian government But he had made a big mistake. He never had to pay this tax in the first place. India and Singapore have a tax treaty called DTAA (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement). Under Article 13(5), capital gains from Indian mutual funds are taxable ONLY in the country where the NRI lives. Singapore does not tax such capital gains. So Varun's actual tax liability in India was ZERO. He had paid ₹1.70 lakh for nothing. When he tried to file a revised return to claim the refund, the deadline had already passed. He wrote to the tax officer requesting a refund. The officer refused: "Too late. You should have claimed this benefit when you filed your original return. Now we cannot help you." Varun did not give up. He went to ITAT Pune. His argument was simple: 🔸 DTAA is a treaty right, not a form-filling formality 🔸 He had a valid Tax Residency Certificate 🔸 Courts have allowed similar fresh claims at the appeal stage before He cited two important cases: 🔸 Bombay High Court in Pruthvi Brokers & Shareholders 🔸 Mumbai ITAT in Anushka Sanjay Shah On 12 October 2026, ITAT Pune ruled in his favour. Key findings: 🔸 DTAA benefit is a substantive legal right 🔸 Missing a form deadline cannot defeat a treaty right 🔸 Fresh legal claims can be raised at appeal stage Varun got his ₹1.70 lakh refund. The lesson for every NRI: If you have paid Indian tax on income that your country's DTAA actually protects, that money is NOT lost forever. You can still claim it back, even after missing the revised return deadline. Your DTAA right is a right, not a formality. Case: Varun Hemant Keskar vs ITO, ITA 133/PUN/2026

    An office boy earning ₹3,500/month got a ₹1.47 crore tax demand. His KYC had been misused by his former employer. ITAT finally saved him. Here's what every Indian should know: Ravi Waghela, a Mumbai office boy, gave his KYC and signatures to his employer in 2009 "for employment purposes." The employer secretly opened a fake PAN in Ravi's name, set up a proprietorship (M/s Kingsy Pharma), and operated a bank account using his identity. Years later, the tax dept found the company was used for accommodation entries. They slapped a ₹1.47 crore demand on Ravi, who still earned ₹3,500/month. Ravi had no idea. The Section 148 notice was "affixed" on a locked room in Bhiwandi which had no connection with him. Only when his CIBIL data was pulled did the final notice reach him in Nov 2019. He immediately denied the PAN. He fought it to the ITAT. On 21 September 2026, the Mumbai ITAT ruled: 🔸 Valid service of Section 148 notice is a jurisdictional requirement 🔸 Affixture on a locked room without proof of residence is NOT valid service The ₹1.47 crore demand was fully QUASHED. Important: The ITAT order does NOT address who misused Ravi's KYC. It only ruled on the jurisdictional issue. The broader lesson: 🔸 Never give your KYC and signatures casually 🔸 Keep a record of every entity holding your PAN/Aadhaar 🔸 Review your AIS yearly for unknown transactions Your KYC is your tax liability. Case: Ravi Dilip Waghela vs ITO, ITAT Mumbai, 21 Sept 2026. Like the content? Repost 🔁 Disclaimer: Please consult a tax and legal advisor.

    Your benefits policy is flexible. Is your claims process? Most flexible benefit plans are designed with care. Categories are chosen, limits are set, the policy is approved. Then the first claim arrives. A bill sits in someone's inbox. A spreadsheet gets updated by hand. An employee asks, again, whether the claim went through. Payroll waits for a final list before the cut-off. The policy was flexible. The experience was not. For employees, the claim is the benefit. For HR, the claim is where the work lives. FlexiBuddy lets employees submit and track claims on WhatsApp, gives HR a dashboard to follow progress, and generates payroll reports from FBP usage. Explore FlexiBuddy: taxbuddy.com/flexibuddy How does a claim move through your team today? #FlexibleBenefits #EmployeeBenefits #FlexiBuddy #HR #Payroll
